mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds Rate above 5% over the prior 10 trading days reduces the discount rate applied to expected future earnings, lowering the present value of equity cash flows and thereby driving negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over the previous 10 trading days
failure_condition: In rising-rate regimes, the 20-day forward return is non-negative and statistically indistinguishable from the 5-day return (p > 0.1), or the FEDFUNDS change is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing the S&P 500 forward 5-day return to positive territory.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2,000 in a month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In 30% of similar labor-market strengthening events, the 5-day forward return is non-positive or the correlation between PAYEMS change and SPX return is < 0.3 (spearman).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% suggests accelerating demand growth, which lowers real interest rates via monetary policy accommodation, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Over 12 consecutive months of accelerating CPIAUCSL growth, the 20-day forward return is negative on average, or the 5-day and 20-day returns are statistically indistinguishable (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% followed by a rebound exceeding 1% within the next two months creates a 'double-dip' fear signal, triggering a short-term negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates supply-side disruptions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% in month t, then rises > +1% in month t+2
failure_condition: In 20 similar volatility events, the 5-day return is non-negative or the timing of the rebound does not coincide with the observed pattern (time-to-rebound > 2 months).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.5%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to the higher discount rate applied to future earnings.
failure_condition: In high-interest-rate regimes, the 60-day forward return is non-negative in > 70% of such events, or the 3-month FEDFUNDS change is not statistically significant (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (HOUST) below 7 million coinciding with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% indicates a cooling labor market, which reduces optimism about future earnings and produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 7,000,000 while UNRATE rises above 4%
failure_condition: In 40% of cooling episodes, the 20-day forward return is positive or the correlation between HOUST and UNRATE is not statistically significant (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months suggests underutilized monetary policy, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady longer than expected and thereby supporting equity valuations, resulting in a positive 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 50 such low-inflation periods, the 5-day forward return is negative on average, or the 5-day return is not significantly different from the 1-day return (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in weekly retail sales (not in the observable list, so instead: a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained rise in personal consumption (CPIAUCSL) by 1%+ for two months indicates improving demand that offsets supply constraints, pushing the S&P 20-day forward return to positive territory in a 'rebound phase'.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% in month t, then CPIAUCSL rises by > 1% in months t+1 and t+2
failure_condition: In 30 such events, the 20-day forward return remains non-positive or the CPIAUCSL rebound is not followed by a positive return within 20 days (time-to-return > 20).
